newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie bounces, but can't shake bears.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie bounces, but can't shake bears.

text.p: *AUD rallied from 18-month lows as bids from various sources led to a classic short squeeze with stops triggered from $0.7450
*Market still short but analysts note rally stopped well short of recovery and trend stays down while below $0.7570
*Similarly CRB index made modest bounce but major downtrend intact. Base metals turning weak adding to poor outlook
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the local dollar was hovering at US$0.7460/65 following a US$0.7418/23 finish here Tuesday, its lowest close since January 1996.
The currency had lurched from US$0.7445 Tuesday afternoon when Prime Minister John Howard expressed a clear preference for yet lower interest rates.

To the market this smacked of political pressure and stoked concerns the normally staunchly independent Reserve Bank had been leant on to deliver the least policy easing on May 23. Most analysts reckoned a cut was probably justified on economic grounds, but worried any move would now be tainted.
The situation is not helped by the RBA's traditional reticence on policy which has earned it a reputation in markets as one of the most tight-lipped central banks in the major western economies.

The bank formally outlines its thinking on the economy and policy just four times a year and even then the message is sometimes so obscure analysts can divine wildly different conclusions from the same report. The market was especially non plusses in May when in testimony to a parliamentary committee RBA governor Ian Macfarlane said there was no economic gain in another rate cut. A fortnight later the bank eased.
The cut, not surprisingly, came as something of a surprise to the market and dealers now operate on the premise the bank can ease at any time, and probably when least expected.
Such uncertainty was not conducive to a sustained dollar rally and while it lasted analysts saw more risk of reaching the bear target of 73 cents than key resistance at US$0.7570.

The poor performance of commodity prices was also bearish for the currency with copper and aluminium joining gold in the doldrums overnight. The CRB index was already at two-year lows and a dismal technical background pointed to more losses ahead.
